works.title: Where Can I Go Without You

position_in_era.primary_genre_lineage: solo-piano improvisation × jazz × Romantic-classical sustained ostinato
position_in_era.geographic_locus: Köln Opera House (recording) / global ECM circuit
position_in_era.historical_role: The single best-selling solo-piano jazz album in history and the public template for what 'solo piano holding a long form together with a sustained left-hand ostinato over which a singing right hand develops a melisma' sounds like — the structural blueprint Spanish music press repeatedly compares Dorantes' *Orobroy* to. Jarrett is one of the two jazz-piano voices (with Bill Evans) that Spanish flamenco-piano press treats as default reference.

narrative_slots.production_facts: Recorded live at the Köln Opera House on 24 January 1975; released on ECM later that year. The piano available was a smaller, partially broken house instrument — Jarrett initially refused to play it.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Solo. The recording is improvised in real time with no prior composition.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: ECM's European jazz aesthetic — high-fidelity, spacious, 'air around the notes' — provides the production grammar that solo-piano flamenco later inherits.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Solo grand piano (in fact a smaller Bösendorfer baby grand mistakenly delivered, with broken upper register and weak pedals — a constraint Jarrett worked around by emphasising mid-register ostinatos).
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: Released 1975 on ECM; over 4 million copies sold; standing reference for solo jazz piano in Europe. The user's red-heart 2023-10-23 hit on Jarrett's *Where Can I Go Without You* (from *Jasmine*) confirms direct in-library presence of the vocabulary.
